pitch.angle: Developers assume companies build software to sell finished apps. In reality, modern tech giants print billions by putting digital tollbooths on individual lines of background code.
key_facts: An API key is a unique string that authenticates and tracks calls between separate software systems.
Twilio generated over one billion dollars in revenue by charging fractions of a cent per SMS API call for apps like Uber.
OpenAI bills developers per text token processed through their API endpoints rather than selling raw software downloads.
Metered rate limiting lets API providers throttle free users while automatically billing paid users based on live consumption.

pitch.title: How Paper Defeated Gold
pitch.hook: In seventeen ninety-two, a single paper dollar was a physical receipt for twenty-four grains of pure gold.
pitch.angle: People assume paper money naturally lost its gold value because gold ran out. In reality, governments issued more paper receipts than the physical metal in their vaults, forcing them to cut the link entirely.
key_facts: In seventeen ninety-two, the United States defined one dollar as twenty-four point seven five grains of pure gold.
Early paper dollars were written receipts for physical metal sitting in bank vaults.
In nineteen thirty-three, President Franklin Roosevelt made holding gold coins illegal for private citizens.
On August fifteen, nineteen seventy-one, President Richard Nixon officially suspended the dollar's convertibility into gold.
pitch.visual_style: painterly historical illustration, dramatic chiaroscuro lighting, muted earth tones, aged paper texture, museum-diorama depth
pitch.style_reason: Gives historical currency transitions an authoritative, museum-grade storytelling atmosphere.
